scope: Connected real load, committed-store, MMIO-store and arbiter engines with conservative single ownership and head-only issue/results. Prepared descriptor producer, core issue/ROB/event retirement, admission producer, LSQ, forwarding and caches are not connected; no full-core or physical timing acceptance.
descriptor: The producer offers an immutable, legal prepared descriptor with desc_valid_i and holds it until desc_take_o or a winning producer cancellation. Full 13-bit ID, attributes, naturally aligned address (unless faulted), size, word-relative mask and already shifted/masked store bytes obey load_store_prepare. Successful loads provide their read byte mask; faults have zero mask/bytes and exact fault address. The producer retains original instruction/PC/operands for later commit-event construction. Load and faulted/uncached store acceptance launches the respective engine; a successful cacheable store remains in the producer until atomic commit_accept_o. No redundant cached-store descriptor buffer is added. desc_take_o is final consumption, not merely readiness.
ordering: The producer must offer memory descriptors in program order, never a younger one that would occupy the only engine slot ahead of an older unissued memory operation. Core IQ ordering is not implemented by this module. Engine/port occupancy plus global fatal blocks every new descriptor and store commit. All nonfaulting load/MMIO reservations require exact live ROB-head ID, issue_allowed_i, no kill and no winning recovery. head_only_i still passes to the load engine unchanged; the conservative additional head policy lives in reservation qualification. issue_allowed_i is a pre-grant stop, not sampled bus readiness; later withdrawal cannot retract an offered request. The committed store reserves independently after retirement and blocks younger loads until its response. No forwarding or speculative memory overlap.
reservation: One pending bit tracks a nonfaulting accepted load/MMIO store before arbiter grant; engine state owns occupancy. Grant directly drives the selected issue_allowed input and is irrevocable. MMIO authorize must equal grant. A selected request follows the grant on the next cycle. No request-valid path depends combinationally on raw target response-valid. Port response routing uses recorded engine ownership, not independently allocated transaction IDs.
retirement: commit_ready_o requires the live cached-store descriptor, empty connected path, exact head/admission IDs, no recovery/kill/fatal, and no raw target response. admit_valid_i/admit_id_i must come from a real producer guaranteeing permissions/refills/resources and no subsequent architectural write fault, as specified by committed_store.json. Never tie admission high in production without establishing that guarantee. commit_i is an accepted pulse legal only with commit_ready_o; commit_accept_o and desc_take_o must coincide with future atomic solo ROB/event/counter retirement. That wiring is outside this task.
result: valid_o requires a held load or MMIO-store result, exact current live ROB-head identity, no effective cancellation/fatal/reset and no raw target response. Result fields are zero while invalid. byte_mask_o gives load read lanes or successful MMIO-store write lanes; faulted results have zero mask/write data. take_i is final owner consumption and must coincide with future atomic solo retirement or fault/trap acceptance. recovery_i does not gate result acceptance: a result/trap-induced recovery may coincide with take_i. A recovery that kills this owner must also assert kill_i and cannot take it. take_i and kill_i are mutually exclusive.
recovery: recovery_i means a recovery wins this cycle and blocks descriptor acceptance, new reservations and store commit. kill_i is externally qualified to the current uncommitted owner and also blocks new acceptance; it cancels a preoffer load/MMIO/local-fault result or drains an offered cached load without returning a result. Repeated kill during a killed-read drain and kill/recovery during a committed-store drain are legal; they never retract traffic. Trap acceptance of this owner is take_i, not kill_i. Any kill after MMIO grant is a caller error, including a faulted MMIO-load result. A wrapper bit preserves uncached-load irrevocability through success/fault take, beyond the standalone load engine flag. Global fatal gates engine kill/take/commit/launch so a healthy engine cannot silently abandon ownership after another block becomes fatal.
ownership: busy_o includes every engine, the port and global fatal. Only reset can clear fatal drain blockage. owner_valid_o/owner_id_o expose whichever engine reports busy; committed_o identifies already retired store ownership and irrevocable_o identifies offered MMIO architectural ownership (not committed-store drain). A fatal load engine suppresses its own busy/owner output, so its owner_valid/id may disappear, but global busy/fatal remain asserted. Arbiter-only fatal freezes otherwise healthy engine ownership. Fatal never permits new acceptance. Precommit cached-store ownership stays upstream and is not counted in busy_o.
fatal: fatal_sources_o bits 0/1/2/3 are load/committed-store/MMIO-store/arbiter registered errors. fatal_reason_o packs arbiter reason in bits 7:6, MMIO reason in 5:3 and committed-store reason in 2:0; load has only a fatal flag. Unsolicited/early/duplicate target responses are captured by the arbiter, not broadcast into idle engines. Raw response-valid suppresses result and commit eligibility immediately, closing the same-edge architectural acceptance race. Descriptor consumption alone may coincide with an unsolicited response because it authorizes no memory side effect. Engine response errors become visible after the routed handshake, immediately stop further grants, and latch the arbiter client-fatal diagnosis on the next edge. No retry or fabricated precise exception for postcommit/protocol errors.
reset: All engines and arbiter share synchronous reset, with channels/visible ownership suppressed while reset is asserted. The target must suppress all pre-reset responses. Reset can lose an already retired but undrained store; it is not normal cancellation or a promise to undo device effects. Qualification paths from raw response to retirement, and head identity to grant to engine state, require later clock review.
verification: Reuse the shared unit runner and packing/schema helpers. The connected bench uses real engines, a byte-addressed target memory and external handshake/ownership checks. Focus on cross-engine ordering, cancellation, protocol routing and retirement gating; standalone unit/formal evidence remains necessary. Random runs vary legal classes, sizes, addresses, data and delays; recovery/fatal/reset/identity edge cases are directed. This is not integrated core instruction execution or an exhaustive formal proof.
